answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by charging a toll at every identity's inlet: each new account must lock a small stake before it may trade or earn. Like bees surrendering a drop of nectar at the hive mouth, a sybil farmer spawning a thousand clones must fund a thousand tolls, and the voyage to profit lengthens with every fake identity. Proven collusion slashes the stake, so the attack costs far more than the nectar it chases.
